correctness.rationale: An independent enumeration using d_U=5−LCS checked all 7140 unordered pairs, yielded 4020 four-cliques, and found that none has a common neighbor outside the clique; this both attains four and excludes every larger code. It counted 134 through 12345 and reproduced the 24 orbits, of sizes 60 (5), 120 (7), and 240 (12), under the 240 distinct relabeling/reversal transformations. Both transformations preserve LCS, they commute, and reversal is not a single symbol relabeling on all words. For a separate check of equidistance, distance 4 means a reversed pair (all symbol pairs have opposed order). After relabeling the pair as increasing and decreasing, a third compatible word would have increasing and decreasing subsequences of lengths at most two. The two lengths ending at each position must form five distinct pairs in {1,2}², impossible. Thus any code of size at least three is already equidistant.
residual_risks: Independent replay uses the stated LCS metric identity rather than a second shortest-path reconstruction. No claim about the full isometry group is audited or needed.
